name: malic
description: Deep research project: massive agentic autonomous loops and intersecting chains. Goal: understand how to safely run autonomous agent loops at scale (dynamic self-delegation, retry/refine loops, budget & termination control) and how intersecting chains (fan-out/join, DAG orchestration, cross-agent shared state) compose without deadlock, runaway cost, or divergent state. ANCHOR (2026-09-08): 'the MALIC machine' = a learning braid — rings (loops) spin independently and share members; overlapping rings and stacked sets mean every agent sits at multiple intersections; when shared members collide they exchange newly-learned success/failure knowledge, so one failure on ring 1 teaches ring 3 in the same iteration. OPERATIONS MODEL (2026-09-08, Jayson): AGS-OS IS THE CHAINS — AGS supplies the agents needed to OPERATE MALIC; 300 mem20agentz workers ARE the chain patterns (C1-C7) that drive the rings. Closed engine: AGS builds/supplies the natives → the braid runs them as rings → collisions produce lessons → 00_reference_store (the fountain, under hypo-map-1) accretes them → AGS trains the next generation from the fountain → re-supplies the braid. Knowledge compounds from real collisions, never imported from static corpora. mem20 is the SERVER-LIFETIME ledger (not project-scoped) remembering every bit, so rings never start blank; proof = measurable improvement over server life (failure rate trends down, skills accrete). Notebook-driven: live Jupyter kernel, findings saved back into mem20 memory.
